content.comment_body: Hello, I have a project that requires reading temperatures up to 300°C. Since there are only two sensors and I prefer a simple setup, I considered using [product_name]. According to the datasheet, [product_name] can handle up to 200°C with an extension module using 0-10V analog input. However, my sensor provides 0-10V output and measures up to 300°C. Is it possible to use this sensor with [product_name]? What issues might arise if I proceed? Thanks!

That information isn't accurate. The [product_name] can measure temperatures from -50 to 200°C with its analog expansion module for RTD sensors. If you use an external measurement transducer with analog output (0-10V or 0/4-20mA), then [product_name] can evaluate whatever temperature range the transducer provides. For instance, with a transmitter covering 0 to 400°C, you could get: - 0-10V or 0-20mA signals with resolution of 0.4°C per unit - 4-20mA signals with resolution of 0.5°C per unit.

[product_name] is capable of reading any analog signal within 0-10V or 4-20mA. The key requirement is a transducer that converts your desired temperature range (0-300°C) into a compatible analog signal, such as 0-10V or 4-20mA.
That essentially matches what was written in my previous comment above yours.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants examined the ability of [product_name] to read high-temperature values beyond what’s stated in the documentation. Clarifications were made that while the analog expansion modules using RTD sensors have a defined range, connecting suitable external transducers outputting standard analog signals (0-10V or 4-20mA) expands the measurable range according to the transducer’s specifications. The discussion highlights the flexibility of the system and notes that the main constraint is within the signal range of the chosen transducer, not the [product_name] itself.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to use [product_name] hardware to directly interpret analog signals (0-10V) from a 0-300°C sensor with reliable hardware performance and maintained measurement accuracy.
